summary: DELTA SIGNAL 2.0 is an interactive Earth Observation WebGIS and Climate Intelligence system designed to detect, quantify, and forecast multi-decadal urban heat island (UHI) expansion and vegetation dynamics across Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Leveraging 24 years (2001–2024) of NASA satellite records (MODIS NDVI, Land Surface Temperature, GPM IMERG Precipitation, and MERRA-2 Atmospheric Reanalysis) alongside 12 high-resolution Landsat 30m composites, we establish rigorous Seasonal Mann-Kendall trend tests and Sen's slope estimations. To bridge historical diagnosis with future climate resilience, we trained an XGBoost machine learning model validated against out-of-sample observations (RMSE 1.077 °C) to generate monthly climate projections through 2030 with 95% confidence intervals. Our platform equips urban planners with actionable spatial insights—revealing a +0.94 °C/decade warming rate in expanding urban corridors and highlighting critical ecological cooling zones to safeguard tropical megacities.
details:
The Problem

Rapid urban development can alter vegetation cover, land surface temperature, and local environmental conditions. However, understanding these changes requires combining long-term satellite observations with reliable spatial and statistical analysis.

Our Solution

DELTA SIGNAL 2.0 is an interactive WebGIS and climate intelligence platform focused on Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, during 2001–2024.

The system integrates NASA Earth observation datasets, high-resolution Landsat imagery, geospatial trend analysis, and an XGBoost machine learning model to investigate environmental change.

How It Works

Satellite observations are screened for quality, spatially processed, and organized into consistent time series. Mann–Kendall and Seasonal Mann–Kendall tests assess long-term trends, while Sen's slope estimates their rates of change.

The platform allows users to explore environmental indicators, compare urban and rural areas, examine satellite-derived land cover changes, and review machine learning predictions.

Main Features

Interactive WebGIS: Explore environmental maps, vegetation indices, land surface temperature, precipitation, and regional comparisons.

Trend Detection: Identify statistically significant environmental trends using Mann–Kendall tests and Sen's slope.

Landsat Analysis: Explore vegetation and built-up surface characteristics using 30-meter satellite imagery.

AI Prediction: Use XGBoost regression to estimate land surface temperature based on historical environmental observations.

Data Quality: Examine observation limitations, missing data, quality indicators, and methodological documentation.

Technologies

The project uses Python, FastAPI, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Google Earth Engine, geospatial data-processing libraries, Plotly, and XGBoost.

Innovation and Impact

The platform combines environmental monitoring, statistical trend detection, regional comparison, and machine learning within a single geospatial investigation environment.

It makes complex Earth observation information more accessible to researchers, students, and urban planners, supporting climate awareness and evidence-informed sustainable urban development.

Scientific Limitations

MODIS and atmospheric reanalysis datasets have spatial-resolution limitations. Statistical associations do not independently establish causation, and machine learning forecasts depend on the quality and representativeness of their training data.
